question: Among the committed dry-pasta case records, which bronze-die pasta under 100 EUR in total is cheapest per kilogram?
use_case: A household buying dry pasta for regular weekday cooking with a hundred-euro purchase budget, who wants the cheapest bronze-die pasta by weight among the packs that budget admits. Eligibility on one dimension and ordering on another; the point of this study is that the budget has no executable control and must not be routed through the per-kilogram cap.

constraints.cost_basis: The listed price of the pack, divided by its validated net weight. Delivery is not included: these records carry no shipping data.

freshness.note: The records are a committed regression case set, not a fresh crawl. Their prices were current when the case set was built and are kept fixed so that this study reproduces; they are not an offer anyone can accept.

assumptions.default: Require the claim, and count the listings that are silent about it separately from those that are ranked.
assumptions.if_wrong: Eight of the twenty-two classified records state it; requiring it removes fourteen that may well be bronze-die and simply do not say so. Drop require_claims to rank the whole shelf.
assumptions.statement: Bronze-die extrusion is worth requiring, and a listing that does not mention it does not have it.

assumptions.default: Rank on price per kilogram regardless of pack size.
assumptions.if_wrong: The leader is a nine-kilogram case of eighteen packs. A household that cannot store that wants a pack-size limit, which would change the order.

questions.answer: Yes — the only marketplace this repository validates.
questions.question: Amazon.de with delivery in Germany?

limits: A vendor's bronze-die statement is a claim the page makes, quoted on the evidence card. It is not an independently verified property of the pasta.
Search does not enumerate a shelf. These twenty-five records were selected because they exercise particular validation rules.
The 100 EUR purchase budget is recorded in the plan and enforced by nothing in this study; the intake section says so.
unacceptable: Fresh pasta — the category classifier excludes it, and it is a different product.
